author: Wil Day
title: 'I shouldn't have done it': Affidavit details alleged Wichita car theft, scuffle with police - NewsBreak
text:
By Wil Day ,
5 hours ago
WICHITA, Kan. (KSNW) — The arrest affidavit of a man accused of assaulting a Wichita police detective in March was released Wednesday.
Dayten Pollard, 18, is charged with two counts of aggravated assault of a law enforcement officer, burglary, theft and interference with law enforcement.
He was arrested on March 17 outside a north Wichita motel after a struggle in which a police detective suffered injuries to his face.
18-year-old charged in assault of police detective at Wichita motel The affidavit says shortly after 7 a.m. that day, a man reported his Mercedes C300 stolen from his home. He said he had left it running with the keys inside outside his home on 15th Street. When it was taken, a bicycle was left nearby, the affidavit says.
A detective who was in an unmarked vehicle near Ninth Street and Broadway Avenue spotted the Mercedes leaving a parking lot of a motel. The detective followed the car to another motel near Broadway and 13th Street, where it pulled into the parking lot just before 7:30 a.m.
Two minutes later, police said a Wichita police officer in a marked vehicle pulled into the parking lot, and he and the detective confronted Pollard and another man.
The affidavit alleges that he had a set of keys in his hand and told police, “He gave me the keys; he gave me the keys.”
The detective looked inside the vehicle to make sure no one else was inside, and police said Pollard then tried to get away from the officer, dropping the keys during the attempt.
Kansas girl’s autopsy released after mom is charged in other child’s death Noticing the struggle, the detective moved to help the officer. But the detective fell as he was reaching for Pollard, the affidavit says, and hit his head on a fire extinguisher box on the outside of the motel.
The officer was able to tackle Pollard to the ground, where police allege he resisted being handcuffed and tried to bite the officer several times.
The affidavit says the officer pulled out his Taser and threatened to use it if Pollard didn’t stop and place his hands behind his back. Pollard appeared to comply at first, but the affidavit says as the officer cuffed his first wrist, Pollard tried to grab the Taser, which the officer had placed on the ground nearby. The officer retrieved the taser and was able to use it to subdue him.
Trial set for man accused of shooting, killing neighbor in Wichita Meanwhile, the detective put out a trouble call for himself and the police officer. Additional officers arrived, and Pollard was taken into custody.
At one point, according to the affidavit, he told officers, “It was stupid, I saw it running, I shouldn’t have done it, I was wrong.”
Later, under questioning by detectives, Pollard admitted that he had gone to the motel to try to find someone to buy the stolen Mercedes, according to the affidavit. He also said he was angry during the arrest and had intended to use the officer’s Taser to get away.
Wichita man arrested in deadly 2024 Seward County crash The detective suffered a serious injury to his face but is recovering.
Pollard made his first court appearance on March 20. He’s scheduled for a preliminary hearing on Monday.
